audit_findings.title: Asbestos is an omitted senior claim unless explicitly embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $127.5m-$275.9m undiscounted damages liability plus $48.5m-$115.3m estimated legal costs through 2065; $8.4m net-of-tax cash outflow in H1 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring settlement and defense cash outflows must reduce OE, or a calibrated liability must be deducted in the equity bridge, without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: The results of the August 31, 2025 study included an estimate of our undiscounted liability for settlement payments and awards of asbestos-related damages, excluding legal costs, ranging from $ 127.5 million to $ 275.9 million for the period through 2065.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a substantial uninsured claim senior to common equity, while the stated bridge contains no asbestos deduction. The record does not establish whether the OE series retained the discontinued-operation cash outflows. If it did not, the omission is reasonably capable of changing the $776m-$998m equity-value range because even the filed low-end damages estimate is 13%-16% of that range before legal costs.
audit_findings.action: Trace provisions, noncash accruals, settlements, legal expenses, tax effects, and discontinued-operation cash outflows through every OE year; then rerun with either normalized after-tax cash outflows in OE or a discounted liability in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Receivables sales may disguise required working capital financing
audit_findings.mechanism: Factoring accelerates collections and reduces reported receivables; if not neutralized, the working-capital deduction in OE is understated.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to these agreements, we sold $ 978.6 million and $ 884.7 million of receivables for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The $978.6m of 2025 receivables sold demonstrates extensive financing activity, but that sales volume is not itself the valuation overstatement. The record does not show whether the OE computation reconstructed pre-sale receivables. The recurring $45.3m 2025 financing charge was included in SG&A, which addresses its cost but not necessarily the displaced working-capital investment.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct annual receivables and operating cash flow as if the sales had not occurred, retain the financing charges already expensed, and rerun OE using the resulting working-capital changes.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter conflicts with the transformative Nissens acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: Nissens contributed $305.377m of 2025 sales and $26.900m of 2025 segment operating income, versus $35.745m of sales for two months in 2024; purchase consideration was $397.111m
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes the business represented by the historical OE series, the latest OE anchor, acquisition-funded interest expense, and the evidence used to select growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Nissens Automotive was created in the fourth quarter of 2024 following the completion of our acquisition of AX V Nissens III ApS (now known as SMP Nissens III ApS) and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (“Nissens Automotive”) in November 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter break, not merely a possibility: 2025 includes a full year of Nissens, 2024 includes two months, and earlier reported years include none. Because the valuation uses a null perimeter while relying on both the latest anchor and historical volatility, the sustainable OE and growth conclusions are not on a consistent basis. A consistent-perimeter rerun could raise or lower value.
audit_findings.action: Build post-acquisition or filed pro-forma OE with consistent Nissens operations, acquisition financing, purchase-accounting effects, and maintenance reinvestment; then reassess the anchor and all growth scenarios.

audit_findings.title: All cash was treated as excess despite operating and geographic needs
audit_findings.magnitude: $78.629m, or $3.34 per diluted share, is the maximum bridge exposure; $70.1m of cash was foreign at December 31, 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash classified as excess is added dollar-for-dollar to equity value, although required operating cash already supports the forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Foreign cash balances at December 31, 2025 and 2024 were $ 70.1 million and $ 42.5 million , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably adds the entire June 2026 cash balance. The required portion is unresolved, but the possible adjustment is large enough to change the conclusion: removing all $78.629m would reduce each scenario by $3.34 per share, versus values of $32.98-$42.43 and a market price of $41.53.
audit_findings.action: Obtain entity-level June 2026 cash, restrictions, repatriation availability, covenant requirements, seasonal liquidity needs, and minimum operating balances; add only demonstrably distributable surplus cash and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method earnings may lack corresponding reinvestment deductions
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.556m of 2025 equity income; $26.310m carrying value of unconsolidated affiliates at December 31, 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity income can enter earnings-based OE while affiliate capital expenditure and working-capital needs remain outside consolidated cash-flow deductions; distributions or look-through OE should replace unsupported accounting income.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we use the equity method, to include our share of the results of certain affiliates based on our economic interest, our ability to exercise significant influence over the operating or financial decisions of these affiliates or our ability to direct their economic resources.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that equity-method income exists, but it does not establish the affiliates' distributions or owner earnings. The potential distortion is therefore unresolved and cannot be quantified from the record. The zero stakes bridge prevents a separate asset addition but does not prove that the affiliate earnings embedded in OE are cash-supported.
audit_findings.action: Obtain affiliate cash-flow statements, capital expenditures, working-capital changes, debt, ownership percentages, and distributions; replace equity income with distributions or proportionate look-through OE and rerun without separately adding the same stake.

audit_findings.title: The anchor depends on a segment with ineffective financial-reporting controls
audit_findings.mechanism: An undetected Nissens classification or measurement error could alter the 2025 OE anchor and consequently every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: A material weakness related to ineffective IT general controls, arising from the unavailability of information to track and monitor administrative user activity has been identified and included in management’s assessment.
audit_findings.explanation: The material weakness is demonstrated and remained unremediated at June 30, 2026, but no financial-statement error attributable to it was identified, and the audited 2025 statements received an unqualified opinion. The record therefore establishes elevated measurement risk, not a valuation misstatement or its direction.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent remediation disclosures, audit adjustments, restatements, and Nissens source-data reconciliations for revenue, margins, inventory, returns, access activity, and acquisition accounting; rerun only if a quantified OE-affecting error is identified.
